note: a tick per step; inputs in plan B units: rate_cd_s / 100 degrees per second, accel_cg / 100 g, course_cd / 100 degrees, fused value [heading_cd, roll_cd, pitch_cd] / 100 degrees, mag counts, now_ms after setup; flags exact, angles in degrees within 0.1 the short way around

cases.name: mirror_an_outranking_source
cases.note: test_attitude: while a priority-0 source (the HITL sim) is fresh the filter COPIES it -- roll and pitch already centidegrees, the heading float degrees -- and does not free-run; once it goes stale the seeded filter free-runs from the copy.

cases.name: free_run_integrates_the_gyro
cases.note: test_attitude: the accelerometer present but outside the 1 g band (no correction): roll, pitch and yaw integrate the rate, +10, -5 and +20 degrees over a second of 20 ms ticks.

cases.name: the_accel_pulls_toward_gravity
cases.note: test_attitude: at rest at roll 30 the gravity vector pulls roll toward it over 40 ticks; then a high-g reading (boost, ~4.2 g) is rejected and the estimate holds.

cases.name: the_turn_gate_holds_the_bank
cases.note: test_attitude: banked 40 degrees with the accelerometer reading level (a coordinated turn) and a 30 degree/s yaw rate, the correction is gated off and the bank holds; at 1 degree/s (straight-ish) gravity re-anchors roll to level.

cases.name: yaw_follows_the_ground_track
cases.note: test_attitude: moving, yaw is pulled to the GNSS track (90 degrees); below the course gate the track is ignored and the gyro alone holds yaw.

cases.name: the_track_pull_wraps_through_north
cases.note: test_attitude: a track just past north pulls a yaw of 358 degrees UP through 360, not back down.

cases.name: a_silent_primary_hands_over_to_the_gyro
cases.note: test_attitude: the priority-0 source pushes once and goes silent. Plan B's read() then answers its extrapolated value with no source, which the filter must not mirror (it once did, pinning a dead heading after every >40 ms gap): it free-runs the 30 degree/s yaw instead.

cases.name: blind_without_a_backup_keeps_publishing
cases.note: test_attitude: 1..4 gyro-less ticks are a GC pause or a stall; the fifth raises blind (logged once). With nothing fresh below the filter it keeps publishing its held estimate. One fresh sample ends blind. A stale channel -- a value with no source -- is no gyro either.

cases.name: blind_while_mirroring
cases.note: test_attitude: the blind window is counted in either regime, so the flag is true before a handover.

cases.name: never_mirror_a_backup_or_a_peer
cases.note: test_attitude: a source ranked BELOW the filter (the BNO055 backup) winning a tick is never copied -- its heading is in another frame; neither is a peer at the filter's own rank, nor the filter's own last push winning.

cases.name: blind_with_a_fresh_backup_withholds
cases.note: test_attitude: no false withhold on 1..4 gyro-less ticks; the fifth withholds so the channel goes stale and the databoard hands the attitude to the fresh backup. A backup that went quiet too gets the publish back. The gyro back: the filter resumes.

cases.name: never_seeded_and_no_accel_publishes_nothing
cases.note: Corner: a filter no source ever seeded runs only while the accelerometer is fresh. Without it the tick publishes nothing AND integrates nothing -- the gyro of that tick is lost, not deferred -- and `free` keeps its last value: nothing clears it.

cases.name: a_long_gap_integrates_one_nominal_period
cases.note: Corner: a gap over 500 ms (an asyncio stall) integrates one nominal period instead of one huge step the yaw would hold for good; exactly 500 ms is integrated whole; a repeated time integrates nothing.

cases.name: the_accel_correction_is_throttled
cases.note: Corner: accel_period_ms 50 at 20 ms ticks pulls every third tick (60 ms apart). A turn neither checks nor restarts the throttle clock, so the first straight tick after it corrects at once.

cases.name: the_gravity_band_edges
cases.note: Corner: the gravity vector is trusted only inside 0.7..1.3 g (squared, so no square root): 0.72 g and 1.29 g pull, 0.68 g and 1.32 g do not.

cases.name: the_magnetometer_carries_yaw_through_a_gnss_dropout
cases.note: test_magnetic_yaw through the tick: while the track is good the magnetometer is MEASURED against it (the offset learned, the mag steering nothing); when the track drops, the learned offset makes the magnetometer a standalone heading and yaw is pulled to it.

cases.name: an_unlearned_magnetometer_never_steers
cases.note: test_magnetic_yaw: with no track ever seen the offset is unlearned -- a zero that would assert magnetic north IS the track -- so the magnetometer must leave yaw alone.

cases.name: the_level_gate_refuses_a_banked_magnetometer
cases.note: test_magnetic_yaw: past mag_level_deg a flat atan2 is not a heading, so a banked or pitched airframe learns nothing from the track; level again, it learns.

cases.name: the_level_gate_reads_the_roll_before_the_gyro_step
cases.note: test_magnetic_yaw's level gate through the tick: plan B gates the magnetometer on the roll it had BEFORE this tick's gyro step (_magnetic_heading runs before blend_cd). Mirrored at roll 14.5 and rolling at 50 degrees/s, the first tick learns -- gated on 14.5 -- although it ends at 15.5; the next starts at 15.5 and refuses. Rolling back, the ticks that start at 16.5 and 15.5 refuse and the one that starts at 14.5 learns again.

cases.name: the_track_needs_the_course_and_the_speed
cases.note: Corner: the GNSS track needs BOTH the course and the ground speed fresh -- plan B drops both when either has no source. The course alone (the speed stale, an extrapolated 14 m/s), then the speed alone (the course stale): no yaw pull, and nothing learned against the magnetometer. Both fresh: the track pulls and the offset is learned.

cases.name: the_accel_pull_goes_the_long_way_round
cases.note: A plan B hazard the port keeps: the accelerometer pull (fixed.blend_cd) takes its error UNWRAPPED. Mirrored at roll 170, then gravity at roll -170 (inverted, inside the 1 g band): the short way is 20 degrees, but the error is -340, so at corr_shift 2 the roll sweeps 85, 21, -27, -62, -89, -109 through wings-level, and only then settles on -170.

cases.name: a_long_free_run_is_exact
cases.note: Corner: 20 s of pure gyro integration -- 1000 ticks of 20 ms at (30, -20, 30) degrees/s, the accelerometer outside the band, no track, no magnetometer -- sweeping roll and yaw 600 degrees and pitch 400. Plan B integrates whole-degree rates over 10 ms multiples exactly, so the 0.1 degree tolerance resolves a gyro step wrong by under 0.02 %. It starts at roll 0.3 and pitch 0.2, so no published roll or pitch sits on the +/-180 wrap.

cases.name: config_default_on_the_pad
cases.note: config_default's own settings (accel_period_ms 50, corr_shift 4) on a level pad: a source seeds the attitude above level and the 1/16 pull brings it down; the blind window, with no backup and then with a fresh one.

cases.name: config_default_a_slow_roll
cases.note: config_default's settings: a 5 degree/s roll on a level gravity vector, under the 4 degree/s turn gate on yaw, so every third tick pulls it back toward level.
